title: Beef & Bean Burritos
subtitle: mild seasoned beef, refried beans, rice and cheddar rolled in big tortillas and toasted crisp
imageAlt: Two golden toasted burritos, one cut to show beef, beans, rice and cheese, with sour cream and salsa on a navy napkin
servingsNote: 8 burritos: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus lunches

breakdown: Onion, garlic, spices, tomato paste, oil

beforeYouStart.text: Start the rice first; it needs to cool a little before rolling.
Warm the tortillas before rolling so they don't crack.

steps.title: Rice
steps.text: Bring the rice and water to a boil with a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Beef
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then add the beef and cook, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Spoon off the fat.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, dried oregano, tomato paste and salt for 1 minute, then the water. Simmer 3–4 minutes until saucy, not wet.

steps.title: Warm the beans and tortillas
steps.text: Warm the refried beans in the microwave 1–2 minutes, stirring once. Wrap the tortillas in a damp towel and microwave 45 seconds until soft.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Spread each tortilla with beans, then add rice, beef and cheddar down the middle. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Wipe out the skillet and toast the burritos seam side down over medium, 2–3 minutes a side, until golden. Serve with the salsa and sour cream.

fixIt.fix: Warm them until soft and floppy, and don't overfill; about ⅔ cup filling each.
Toast seam side down first; it seals them.
Simmer the beef until the water has nearly cooked off before rolling.

saleTip: Large tortillas and refried beans are often on the No Frills flyer together; old cheddar blocks beat bags.
swap: Ground turkey: same method, cooked to 74°C (165°F).
leftovers: Wrap cooled burritos individually in foil; they make the best grab-and-go lunches.
doneness: Ground beef cooked to 71°C (160°F) with no pink (Health Canada). Reheat burritos to 74°C (165°F) in the centre.
source: Based on tested beef and bean burrito methods (Canadian Living, Budget Bytes): mildly seasoned ground beef, refried beans, rice and cheese, rolled and toasted in a dry skillet.
prepAhead: The beef and rice keep 3 days in the fridge; roll fresh.
Roll extra burritos, wrap individually and freeze.
reheat: From the fridge: foil-wrapped at 180°C (350°F) 20 minutes. From frozen: unwrapped in the microwave 2 minutes a side, then crisp in a skillet. Hot to 74°C (165°F) in the centre.

basic.note: Beef, beans and cheese; no rice, cumin or dried oregano.

stepNotes.2: Basic: chili powder, paprika, tomato paste and salt.
stepNotes.4: Basic: beans, beef and cheddar only.

fancy.note: Smothered and baked under salsa and melted cheese, with guacamole.

stepNotes.5: Fancy: instead of toasting, set the burritos seam side down in a 9×13-inch (23×33 cm) baking dish, spoon the extra salsa over and cover with the mozzarella. Bake at 200°C (400°F) 15 minutes until bubbling.

addSteps.title: Guacamole
addSteps.text: Mash the avocados with the lemon juice and salt and serve on the side.

plating: One burrito cut on the diagonal to show the inside.
Sour cream and salsa in small bowls.

why.2-0: Refried beans glue the filling together and keep it moist.
why.1-4: Regular chili powder is a mild blend of ground chilies, cumin and dried oregano; it adds flavour, not heat.
why.0-0: Rice stretches the beef and soaks up the juices so the burrito isn't soggy.

funFact: 'Burrito' means 'little donkey' in Spanish, possibly for the way it carries its load.

keeps.note: wrap each burrito in foil, then bag
